Programmable device controllers are gradually becoming a key part of advanced users' workflows, including agentic programming. Logitech is now officially bringing a compact solution to market that fits anywhere on your desk.

Logitech today announced the MX Keypad, an accessory priced at US$99.99, featuring 9 customisable full-colour LCD keys for quickly launching commands, executing macros and opening AI tools.

The MX Keypad is half the price of the Logitech MX Creative Console.

If the hardware looks familiar to you, there's a reason. Logitech's MX Creative Console pairs an LCD keypad with a separate dial controller (dialpad), making it easy to adjust settings and operate within creative applications.

The MX Keypad retains only the keypad experience, without the extra controller, and is only half the price of the Creative Console's US$199.99 tag.

The new product's marketing focus is on developers and AI workflows, though the customisation features actually extend beyond coding.

The experience can be customised through the Logi Options+ app.

Through the free Logi Options+ app, users can assign hotkeys, pre-stored prompts, scripts and macros to individual keys. The device has two page-switching buttons, supporting up to 15 pages of settings, while app-aware functionality automatically switches profiles as you move between different apps.

This means the same set of physical keys can perform different roles in VS Code, Slack, Chrome or other applications. The Logi Marketplace offers various plugins, profiles and icon packs, and the built-in icon editor lets users customise the appearance of each key.

You can use AI to build your own AI keypad.

My initial hands-on test involved connecting the MX Keypad to the MacBook Air on my desk, then having Codex use its computer-use capability to create custom keys in Logi Options+ based on how I use ChatGPT on Mac.

Having an AI coding agent set up physical keys for operating AI is somewhat poetic, and it clearly states the product's selling point: putting the prompts and actions you frequently use onto dedicated, labelled keys.

The MX Keypad was developed through a partnership between Logitech and GitHub. The product comes with built-in VS Code integration for GitHub Copilot, and both new and existing users will receive a 3-month free Copilot Pro+ subscription, redeemable through Logi Options+.

The MX Keypad supports third-party community plugins.

Logitech also noted that community-developed plugins for Claude Code and OpenAI Codex offer features such as agent status tracking and terminal control. Developers who want to go further can use the Logi Actions SDK, which supports C# and Node.js, to create custom plugins.

The MX Keypad connects via USB-C and requires macOS 13 or later, or Windows 10 or later. It measures approximately 3.6 x 3.1 inches and weighs just 96 grams, so it won't take up much space next to your laptop or keyboard.

The MX Keypad goes on sale today (8 September) in Graphite and Pale Grey, priced at US$99.99.
